body.title: Add `--include-descendants` to `glab milestone list --group`
body.description:
## Problem

`glab milestone list --group <group>` only returns milestones defined on that group. You can't list milestones from its subgroups or their projects. The command already has `--include-ancestors` for parent groups, but nothing for descendants.

## Proposal

Add an `--include-descendants` flag that sets `include_descendants=true` on [List group milestones](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/group_milestones/#list-group-milestones).

- The flag applies only with `--group`. Reject it with `--project`.
- Show the owning group or project in the output, because results now span namespaces.

## Context

client-go only started sending `include_descendants` in v3.40.1 ([client-go!3164](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/-/merge_requests/3164), which also decodes `project_id` on group milestones). glab picks this up in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4273, so this issue depends on that MR being merged.

Relevant code: `internal/commands/milestone/list/list.go`.

body.title: Unblock snap channel releases pending dot-kube-config store declaration
body.description:
Snap uploads are held for manual review because the `dot-kube-config` `personal-files` plug (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8304) needs a store declaration. Until it's granted, no glab revision reaches the edge or stable channels.

Request: https://forum.snapcraft.io/t/personal-files-request-for-glab-kube-config-write-to-kube/53662. Two reviewers have given +1 for installation-only write access to `$HOME/.kube/config` and `$HOME/.kube/config.lock`, with manual connection. Revision [7045](https://dashboard.snapcraft.io/snaps/glab/revisions/7045/) is the first upload with the final plug, and older held revisions have been rejected.

## Tasks

- [ ] Declaration granted and revision 7045 approved
- [ ] Remove `allow_failure: true` and `retry` from `snapcraft_release_edge` (added in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4132)
- [ ] Get the latest release onto the stable channel. The 1.125.0 upload (revision 7035) was rejected because it had the old plug.

body.title: glab fails when the remote uses the instance's separate SSH hostname, such as ssh.gitlab.gnome.org
body.description:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: glab 1.126.0 (4dd0d32d1)
- [x] Operating system and version: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Linux 7.2.8, x86_64)
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? self-managed (gitlab.gnome.org)
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed): 19.4.5
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues: logged in to gitlab.gnome.org
- [x] Run the command in debug mode: `GLAB_DEBUG=true` only adds a telemetry hook line repeating the same error

### Summary

In a clone whose remote is on `ssh.gitlab.gnome.org`, every repository command fails with "none of the git remotes configured for this repository point to a known GitLab host", although glab is logged in to gitlab.gnome.org. The error says to run `glab auth login`, which was already done.

gitlab.gnome.org serves Git over SSH on that separate hostname, and glab only matches a remote on it to the instance when `ssh_host` is set for the instance.

`glab auth login` only sets it with `--ssh-hostname` or when run interactively inside the clone, so a scripted login, or one done before cloning, leaves it unset.

Workaround: `glab config set ssh_host ssh.gitlab.gnome.org --host gitlab.gnome.org`.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 7.2.8-1-t2-resolute x86_64 (Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS)
- SHELL: /bin/bash
- TERM: xterm-ghostty
- GLAB: glab 1.126.0 (4dd0d32d1)

Other:

### Steps to reproduce

1. `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.gnome.org --stdin < token.txt`
2. `git clone git@ssh.gitlab.gnome.org:GNOME/gnome-settings-daemon.git && cd gnome-settings-daemon`
3. `glab issue list`

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

```plaintext
none of the git remotes configured for this repository point to a known GitLab host. Please use `glab auth login` to authenticate and configure a new host for glab.

Configured remotes: ssh.gitlab.gnome.org.
```

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

glab lists the issues of `GNOME/gnome-settings-daemon` on gitlab.gnome.org, as it does with the workaround.

### Possible fixes

In [`remote_resolver.go`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/c2544a916/internal/cmdutils/remote_resolver.go#L141-155), map an SSH host that is a subdomain of a configured host to that host, unless an `ssh_host` says otherwise. The test "SSH host matches but no ssh_host config — remote skipped" asserts the current behavior; I found no discussion in !2924 that made it deliberate.

I have a merge request ready for this.
